title: Probability and Statistics
description: Averages, spread and chance: core ideas for reasoning about data

questions.question: What is the mean of 2, 4, 4, 5 and 10?
questions.explanation: The mean is the sum divided by the count: (2 + 4 + 4 + 5 + 10) / 5 = 25 / 5 = 5.

questions.question: What is the median of 3, 9, 1, 7 and 5?
questions.explanation: Sort the values (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) and take the middle one: 5.

questions.question: What is the mode of 1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3, 4?
questions.explanation: The mode is the most frequent value. 3 appears three times, more than any other value.

questions.question: What is the probability of rolling a 6 on a fair six-sided die?
questions.explanation: A fair die has six equally likely outcomes and exactly one of them is a 6, so the probability is 1/6.

questions.question: What is the probability of flipping two heads in a row with a fair coin?
questions.explanation: The flips are independent, so multiply: 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

questions.question: A bag holds 3 red and 7 blue marbles. What is the probability of drawing a red marble?
questions.explanation: There are 10 marbles and 3 are red, so the probability is 3/10 = 0.3.

questions.question: What is the range of the data set 4, 12, 7, 19, 2?
questions.explanation: The range is the maximum minus the minimum: 19 - 2 = 17.

questions.question: Which measure of center is least affected by extreme outliers?
questions.explanation: The median only depends on the middle value(s), so a single extreme value barely moves it. The mean is pulled toward outliers.

questions.question: In a normal distribution, roughly what percentage of values fall within one standard deviation of the mean?
questions.explanation: The empirical (68-95-99.7) rule says about 68% fall within one standard deviation, 95% within two and 99.7% within three.

questions.question: What is the probability of an event that is certain to happen?
questions.explanation: Probabilities range from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain). A certain event has probability 1, which is 100% when written as a percentage.
